statement: In year 5 Quraysh and allied tribes, about ten thousand, marched on Madinah; the Qur'an calls them al-Ahzab.
alternatives: Dated Shawwal of year 5 by most; some say year 4.

statement: Salman the Persian suggested digging a trench across the exposed northern side.

Anas: the Emigrants and Ansar dug on cold mornings carrying earth on their backs, with no servants; they chanted their pledge and he replied 'O Allah, there is no good but the good of the Hereafter, so bless the Ansar and the Emigrants'.
notes: Direct speech. 4100 machine-checked; 'cold mornings' and 'no servants' are in 4099, from memory.

statement: Al-Bara: he saw him carrying earth until dust covered his stomach, reciting Ibn Rawahah's lines.
Jabir: they struck a hard rock; he came down with a stone tied to his stomach, as they had not eaten for three days; he struck it and it became like sand.
notes: Machine-checked. The narration continues with the meal at Jabir's house, not narrated here.

statement: The Confederates camped beyond the trench; the siege lasted close to a month.
Banu Qurayzah, bound by treaty, broke it and sided with the besiegers.
He supplicated: O Allah, revealer of the Book, swift in reckoning, defeat the Confederates and shake them.

Hudhayfah: on a night of violent wind and cold he asked who would bring news of the enemy; none answered; he sent Hudhayfah by name, telling him not to provoke them; Hudhayfah entered their camp and returned.
notes: Content machine-checked for the opening in the Muslim dataset (no. 4640); Abd al-Baqi number from memory. The details of the tents and pots and their departure are from the Seerah and longer narrations; reviewer to confirm.

statement: He said: now we shall attack them and they will not attack us; Quraysh never marched on Madinah again.
Banu Qurayzah were besieged and agreed to the judgement of Sa'd ibn Mu'adh, who judged between them.
notes: Machine-checked. The content of the judgement (the fighting men to be killed, the families taken captive) is not stated in the narration script. Reviewer to decide whether omitting it is acceptable or misleading.
